targets.authors: Cai, J., Ran, H., Hwang, S., Ma, Y., Han, J., & Muirhead, F.
targets.title: Impact of prompts on students’ mathematical problem posing.
targets.evidence_quote: The present study aimed to replicate previous research on the impact of problem-posing prompts on students’ mathematical problem posing in the United States (Cai et al., 2023 ) by examining whether similar patterns emerge in two additional educational contexts: Chile and Cyprus.
targets.outcome_quote: In Chile, two complexity measures (linguistic structure and semantic structure) of solvable mathematical problems for two tasks, named Road Trip and Doorbell, were significantly associated with the prompt, but neither of the complexity measures were significantly associated with the prompt for the third task (Animal). In Cyprus, none of the complexity measures were statistically significantly associated with the prompt for any of the tasks. In contrast, in the original study with US students, the linguistic structure of solvable mathematical problems for the Road Trip task was statistically significantly associated with the prompt, but none of the complexity measures were significantly associated with the prompt for the Doorbell and Animal tasks.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit contrast: Chile agrees on Road Trip prompt association but differs for Doorbell; Cyprus differs on Road Trip; null effects agree for Animal. The authors compare countries and tasks to the US original.
